source.user_scenario_text: A second energy shock pushes inflation back above 7% and it stays sticky for a decade. Central banks tolerate 4% rather than force a deep recession.

warnings.message: Average inflation 6.5% with policy rate ending at 7.5% keeps real rates near +1% — coherent, no repression flag. No action needed.

narrative.title: The Long Stagflation
narrative.tagline: 2027–2036: the decade prices refused to behave
narrative.summary: A second energy shock and fractured supply chains push inflation back above 7% in 2027, and this time it does not come quietly. Central banks hike into a stagnating economy, discover the political ceiling on unemployment, and settle for containment over victory. For ten years, cash has a real job, duration is a liability, and the stock-bond correlation that defined a generation of portfolios quietly flips sign.
narrative.lesson: In this world the classic 60/40 loses its diversifier: bonds fall with stocks when inflation drives both. Real assets and floating-rate private credit carry the portfolio, while private equity, built on cheap leverage and multiple expansion, gives back a decade of its advantages.
